descriptionChirho: Masculine noun denoting rebellion, contrariness, or defiant resistance against God or authority. Predominant in Ezekiel's characterization of Israel as a bêt merī 'house of rebellion' (Ezek 2:5-8; 3:9,26-27; 12:2-3,9,25; 17:12; 24:3; 44:6), and in the wilderness narrative (Num 17:10 'children of rebellion'; Dt 31:27 'your rebellion'). Also used in wisdom literature (Prov 17:11 'a rebellious man seeks only evil') and historical reflection (1 Sam 15:23 'rebellion is as the sin of divination'; Job 23:2 'my complaint is rebellion'; Neh 9:17 'in their rebellion'). Multilingual glosses are unanimous: arb ʿiṣyān/tamarrud (disobedience/rebellion), deu Widerspenstigkeit (contrariness), spa rebeldia/rebelion, hin vidroha/baghvat (revolt/rebellion), kor banyeok (rebellion). All inflectional variants (absolute, construct, with article, with suffixes, with prepositions) share this single semantic core.
